items.titleOriginal: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Inflation-Aware Routing for Agentic LLM Systems
items.summaryOriginal: arXiv:2608.13571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a language model fails to answer a query on the first attempt, an agentic system retries, consuming additional tokens each time. This retry overhead creates a gap between what a model's per-token price implies and what a full workflow actually costs. We call this gap \emph{token inflation} and define it as the ratio of true workflow cost to single-call cost. Systems like FrugalGPT route based on the latter, which can underestimate real cost by more than $2\times$ on difficult tasks. We address this with InflationAgent, a four-stage router that (1) measures token inflation systematically across model tiers and task types, finding inflation as high as $4.25\times$ for a 7B model on multi-hop question answering; (2) introduces CoT Branching Entropy (CBE), a pre-execution difficulty signal computed entirely from local inference, which predicts high inflation with AUROC 0.887; and (3) selects models by maximizing a Semantic Exchange Rate (SER) that divides expected accuracy by predicted true cost, with a fresh-escalation policy that discards failed chains before routing to a stronger model. items.detailZh: 该论文针对智能体LLM系统中重试机制导致的token消耗膨胀问题，提出了“token通胀”概念，并设计了InflationAgent路由器。作者首先系统测量了不同模型规模和任务类型下的token通胀，发现7B模型在多跳问答上通胀高达4.25倍。其次，他们提出了CoT分支熵（CBE）作为执行前难度信号，该信号完全由局部推理计算，预测高通胀的AUROC达到0.887。最后，他们通过最大化语义汇率（SER）来选择模型，SER定义为预期准确率除以预测真实成本，并采用新鲜升级策略，在路由到更强模型前丢弃失败的链。在GSM8K固定预算下，InflationAgent相比基线方法在成本效益上有所提升。

items.interpretationZh: 该研究提供了量化证据表明智能体系统的实际成本可能远高于单次调用价格，并提出了一个可行的路由框架。但需要注意的是，结果基于特定模型和任务，泛化性有待验证。

items.summaryOriginal: arXiv:2608.13578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer architectures rely on dense self-attention to model long-range dependencies, but this mechanism exhibits quadratic complexity with respect to sequence length. We introduce BCMT (Blockwise Causal Memory Transformer), an architecture for long-context language modeling that decouples local token interactions from global context propagation. Dense causal self-attention is applied independently within local blocks, while each block produces an adaptive summary aggregated through an exponential causal memory. This memory is subsequently injected back into the token representations, enabling efficient propagation of long-range contextual information without relying on explicit global attention. Unlike standard Transformers and recurrent memory architectures, BCMT maintains neither dense interactions between distant tokens nor learned memory states. Its memory mechanism is fully parallelizable and remains compatible with standard implementations of dense self-attention. Experiments on language modeling with context lengths of up to 1024 tokens show that BCMT achieves validation performance comparable to that of Dense Transformers

items.howItWorksZh: BCMT的工作方式如下：输入序列被划分为多个局部块。在每个块内，应用标准的密集因果自注意力，以捕捉局部token间的依赖关系。每个块在自注意力后产生一个自适应摘要（例如，通过池化或注意力加权）。这些摘要通过指数因果记忆进行聚合，即每个时间步的记忆是之前所有摘要的指数加权和，权重随时间衰减。聚合后的记忆向量被注入回当前块的token表示中（例如，通过加法或拼接），从而为每个token提供全局上下文信息。整个过程可并行化，因为记忆聚合可以按块顺序计算，但块内自注意力可并行。
items.interpretationZh: 论文声称BCMT在1024 token上下文长度下达到与密集Transformer相当的验证性能，同时避免了二次复杂度。这暗示BCMT可能是一种有效的长上下文建模方法。然而，论文仅报告了验证性能，未提供下游任务或更长上下文的评估，因此其实际优势仍需进一步验证。
items.limitationsZh: 论文仅报告了验证性能，未提供下游任务或更长上下文的评估，因此其实际优势仍需进一步验证。

items.summaryOriginal: arXiv:2608.13574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly operate as execution systems that invoke tools, modify local state, use persistent memory, and interact with external protocols. These capabilities make agents useful, but they also introduce risks related to over-privileged actions, weak auditability, prompt injection, tool poisoning, and uncontrolled side effects. This paper presents Agentao, a governed local-first runtime for tool-using LLM agents. Agentao separates model-generated action proposals from host-authorized execution through a layered architecture consisting of host-facing surfaces, a host contract, a runtime core, a permission-mediated tool system, and supporting subsystems for memory, replay, plugins, skills, sub-agents, and protocol integration. We describe the motivation, threat model, design goals, governance model, execution pipeline, and structured event interface of the system. items.titleOriginal: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models
items.summaryOriginal: arXiv:2608.13567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The human brain exhibits a striking degree of functional specialization, with distinct networks supporting language, formal reasoning, reasoning about other minds, and reasoning about the physical world. Is this modular organization a fundamental principle of how intelligent systems must be built, or an evolutionary accident specific to biological brains? Here, we test whether a similar organization emerges in Large Language Models--another class of intelligent systems created through a very different optimization process. Using circuit analyses across N=46 tasks spanning four cognitive domains (language, formal reasoning, social reasoning, physical reasoning), we find that LLMs develop a modular architecture that mirrors the human brain: tasks drawing on the same network in humans recruit overlapping neurons in LLMs, whereas tasks drawing on different networks recruit distinct neurons. The convergent emergence of modularity in brains and neural networks suggests that it may be a fundamental property of intelligent systems.

items.titleOriginal: Depth-Aware Sensitivity Analysis of Mixture-of-Experts Models via Magnitude-Based Expert Masking
items.summaryOriginal: arXiv:2608.13565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale large language models (LLMs) while preserving computational efficiency through sparse activation. Despite their widespread adoption, the relative importance of individual MoE layers remains insufficiently characterized, particularly for model compression. This paper presents a systematic layer-wise sensitivity analysis of the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model (40 MoE layers, 256 experts per layer, top-8 routing) using magnitude-based expert masking on the XLCoST cross-lingual code translation benchmark. We conduct a multi-phase study spanning 100, 300, and 500 prompt evaluation scales across three H100 GPU servers. Our central finding is that layer sensitivity is strongly depth-dependent: early layers (0-9) and middle layers (10-29) are highly fragile to expert masking, while late layers (30-39), and especially very-late layers (35-39), tolerate aggressive masking of low-magnitude experts. Flat all-layer masking at 30% retains only 150/300 Good+Similar outputs at 300-prompt scale, whereas late-focused policies retain 249-255/300 while masking 640-1,145 experts. On a later 500-prompt held-out validation

items.titleEn: Depth-Aware Sensitivity Analysis of Mixture-of-Experts Models via Magnitude-Based Expert Masking
items.summaryZh: 本文对Qwen3.6-35B-A3B模型（40个MoE层，每层256个专家，top-8路由）进行了逐层敏感性分析，使用基于幅度的专家掩码在XLCoST跨语言代码翻译基准上测试。研究发现层敏感性强烈依赖于深度：早期层（0-9）和中间层（10-29）对专家掩码高度脆弱，而晚期层（30-39），尤其是35-39层，能容忍对低幅度专家的激进掩码。在300提示规模下，平坦的全层掩码30%仅保留150/300个Good+Similar输出，而晚期聚焦策略在掩码640-1145个专家时保留249-255/300。在后续500提示的保留验证中，结果类似。
items.summaryEn: This paper presents a systematic layer-wise sensitivity analysis of the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model (40 MoE layers, 256 experts per layer, top-8 routing) using magnitude-based expert masking on the XLCoST cross-lingual code translation benchmark. The study finds that layer sensitivity is strongly depth-dependent: early layers (0-9) and middle layers (10-29) are highly fragile to expert masking, while late layers (30-39), especially 35-39, tolerate aggressive masking of low-magnitude experts. At 300-prompt scale, flat all-layer masking at 30% retains only 150/300 Good+Similar outputs, whereas late-focused policies retain 249-255/300 while masking 640-1,145 experts. On a later 500-prompt held-out validation, results are similar.
items.detailZh: 该研究针对混合专家（MoE）架构的大语言模型，特别是Qwen3.6-35B-A3B模型，进行了逐层敏感性分析。MoE模型通过稀疏激活在保持计算效率的同时扩展模型规模，但各MoE层的相对重要性尚未被充分表征，尤其是在模型压缩方面。研究者采用基于幅度的专家掩码方法，在XLCoST跨语言代码翻译基准上进行了多阶段实验，评估规模包括100、300和500个提示，并使用三台H100 GPU服务器。核心发现是层敏感性强烈依赖于深度：早期层（0-9）和中间层（10-29）对专家掩码高度脆弱，而晚期层（30-39），尤其是35-39层，能容忍对低幅度专家的激进掩码。具体而言，平坦的全层掩码在30%掩码率下，300提示规模仅保留150/300个Good+Similar输出，而晚期聚焦策略在掩码640-1145个专家时保留249-255/300。在后续500提示的保留验证中，结果类似。该研究为MoE模型的压缩和高效部署提供了重要见解。
keyPointsZh: 对Qwen3.6-35B-A3B模型（40个MoE层，每层256个专家，top-8路由）进行了逐层敏感性分析。
使用基于幅度的专家掩码在XLCoST基准上测试，评估规模包括100、300和500个提示。
发现层敏感性强烈依赖于深度：早期层和中间层脆弱，晚期层（尤其是35-39层）能容忍激进掩码。
平坦的全层掩码30%仅保留150/300个Good+Similar输出，而晚期聚焦策略保留249-255/300。
items.impactZh: 该研究揭示了MoE模型中不同层对专家掩码的敏感性差异，为模型压缩提供了新的策略：优先保留早期和中间层的专家，而可以激进地剪枝晚期层的低幅度专家。这有助于在保持模型性能的同时显著减少计算量，对资源受限环境下的模型部署具有重要意义。
items.userImpactZh: 对于AI开发者和研究团队，该研究提供了实用的模型压缩指导：在剪枝MoE模型时，应优先保留早期和中间层的专家，而可以激进地剪枝晚期层的低幅度专家，从而在保持性能的同时减少计算开销。
items.howItWorksZh: 研究者采用基于幅度的专家掩码方法，即根据专家权重的幅度（magnitude）来决定是否掩码（即剪枝）某个专家。他们逐层应用掩码，并评估不同层对掩码的敏感性。实验在XLCoST基准上进行，使用Good+Similar作为性能指标。通过比较平坦的全层掩码和晚期聚焦策略，他们得出了层敏感性随深度变化的结论。
items.interpretationZh: 该研究的结果表明，MoE模型的晚期层对专家掩码的容忍度更高，这可能是因为晚期层更专注于任务特定的细节，而早期层和中间层则负责更基础的特征提取。然而，该研究仅基于一个模型和一个基准，结论的泛化性有待验证。
items.limitationsZh: 该研究仅针对Qwen3.6-35B-A3B模型和XLCoST基准，结论可能不适用于其他MoE模型或任务。此外，掩码策略基于幅度，可能不是最优的剪枝准则。实验规模有限，且未提供与其他剪枝方法的对比。
actionStepsZh: 在压缩MoE模型时，优先保留早期和中间层的专家，而可以激进地剪枝晚期层的低幅度专家。
使用基于幅度的专家掩码作为初步剪枝策略，但需在具体任务上验证。
考虑在更多模型和任务上验证层敏感性结论的泛化性。

visual.insightZh: 晚期聚焦策略在300提示规模下保留的Good+Similar输出数量（249-255）远高于平坦全层掩码（150），表明晚期层掩码更有效。
